PullRequest.Title: Agents: add Move to Session... commands for chats and sessions
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #343906

Adds non-drag-and-drop alternatives for the two moves that previously only the sessions list drag and drop could start:

- **Nested chat row** → "Move to Session..." (`sessions.list.moveChatToSession`, group `1_move` next to Promote to Session): quick pick of valid destination sessions, moves the chat to the end of the chosen session.
- **Single-chat session row** → "Move to Session..." (`sessions.list.moveSessionIntoSession`, group `1_move`): quick pick of valid destinations, nests the session at the end.

How it works:
- The validity rule (`canMoveIntoSession` plus `canMoveChat`/`canMoveSessionUnder`) and the append anchor (skips tool and hidden chats) are now shared helpers in `sessionsListChatMove.ts`, used by both the drag and drop functions and `getChatMoveDestinations`/`getSessionMoveDestinations`. Other provider/agent exclusion comes only from that shared check.
- Moves run through `runSessionsListMove` (progress, notice with Undo, refusal warnings, reveal/select), like Promote to Session.
- Gated on `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled`, `ChatContextKeys.enabled`, the row's can-move key, and a new has-destination context key computed when the menu opens (hidden when there is no destination). `run()` re-validates. No keybinding, not in the Command Palette.
- The quick pick has a descriptive placeholder (announced by screen readers), the session's chat count as detail, and the Agents window accessibility help lists the command.
- The label is a single const (`MOVE_TO_SESSION_LABEL`) so renames are one-line.

Merge note: #343908 makes `ISessionsListMoveOptions.placementServices` required. Whichever PR merges second wires it: if #343908 merges first, this PR passes `placementServices: { sessionsListModelService, sessionGroupsService }` from both actions; if this merges first, #343908 adds it to them. #343907 will conflict mechanically on `getSessionsListChatDrop`/`getSessionsListSessionDrop`.

Validation:
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: ok
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 1014 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.js"`: 57 passing
- `npm run eslint -- <7 changed files>`: clean
- `npm run typecheck-client`: clean
- Mutation checks (sessionType check, supportsMultipleChats check, setting in `when`, has-destination key): each made a test fail.
- Live (full build, seeded authenticated throwaway profile, Claude/Codex off, keyboard only via Shift+F10 and the quick pick, real Copilot sessions): (1) chat row → "Move to Session..." → picker listed only the other session (not its own parent) → chat moved to the end of it; the notice has Undo and Undo moved it back ("Moved ... back into ..."). (2) single-chat session row → "Move to Session..." (7th item) → picker "Move 'Reply OK-C' into Session" listed the other sessions with "1 chat" and not itself → nested as the last chat, notice with Undo; Undo restored the session. (3) after marking a session Done it no longer appears as a destination (other-agent exclusion is covered by unit tests; Claude/Codex were off). (4) with no valid destination left, the item is hidden on the chat row. (5) A refusal showed the warning notice "Could not move session ... This chat can't be moved." (seen earlier on a not-ready provider). Orderings not exercised live.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path and all-session cardinality are explicit in the changed lines and helper implementations, and the setting gate is demonstrably only in the menu when-clause after overlay construction. Exact delay varies with history size and providers, but that affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread CPU work and temporary arrays/destination objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each session or nested-chat context-menu open now rebuilds the merged session list across all providers and then traverses every session; every eligible target also calls getChatMoveAppendAnchor, whose scan grows with trailing hidden/tool chats. This is O(all known sessions plus inspected target chats), not the five rows per group normally rendered by the capped list.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased context-menu opening latency and possible UI jank for users with large agent-session histories
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, opening these context menus did not call ISessionsManagementService.getSessions or enumerate possible move targets; destination work only existed for an actual drag target.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added context keys synchronously call getSessionMoveDestinations/getChatMoveDestinations and materialize the complete destination array before the menu can be shown, merely to test length > 0. This runs even when chat moves are disabled and the command's when-clause will hide it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 7365 newly invokes getSessionMoveDestinations(element, this._sessionsManagementService.getSessions(), ...).length during context-menu construction; RIGHT line 7456 adds the same full enumeration for chat menus. Neither call existed before this diff.
Findings.Title: Avoid enumerating every destination while opening the context menu
Findings.Impact: Right-clicking any session row (and, via the analogous added line 7456, any nested chat row) can stall menu display while all provider sessions are merged, deduplicated, and scanned. The trigger is especially broad on Stable, where the move setting defaults off but this work still runs.
Findings.Evidence: onContextMenu and showChatContextMenu build their overlays synchronously before contextMenuService.showContextMenu. The added line calls getSessions(), whose implementation merges every provider's getSessions result and deduplicates it; getSessionMoveDestinations uses flatMap over that entire result, and getChatMoveAppendDestination computes getChatMoveAppendAnchor for each valid target. SessionsList already keeps the current uncapped collection in this.sessions, while rendering caps groups to DEFAULT_SESSION_GROUP_LIMIT=5, so a large hidden history still participates. No subprocess/IPC/network call is awaited on the normal warm path; the regression is synchronous CPU/allocation on menu display.
Findings.Recommendation: Gate this computation with the existing move-enabled/ChatContextKeys condition, reuse the SessionsList's cached this.sessions collection, and add an existence-only helper using some(canMoveIntoSession) so menu construction stops at the first valid target without computing append anchors or allocating destination objects. Keep full destination/anchor construction in the command after the user selects it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a session-row or nested-chat context menu in the Sessions list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Overlay construction, including the newly added destination computation, runs synchronously before createMenu/showContextMenu, so all enumeration must finish before the menu appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent-host listSessions refresh, only if a provider cache is still uninitialized
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight request per uninitialized provider because _sessionRefreshInFlight and retry guards coalesce it; normally zero because list construction already warmed the cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Context-menu construction did not call ISessionsManagementService.getSessions, so it could not newly reach this refresh from the menu path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is started asynchronously and is not awaited by context-menu construction; the reportable regression is the synchronous local enumeration and allocation, not IPC latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All known sessions from all registered local, remote, backend, and cloud providers, not just the five sessions normally rendered per capped group; eligible target sessions may additionally scan trailing hidden/tool chats to find an append anchor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the UI thread; there is no limiter or yielding because the work is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider session models are normally warm because SessionsList.refreshSessions already populated them, but every call still allocates provider arrays, a merged/deduplicated array, and a full destination array. There is no destination cache or early-exit existence check. On an uninitialized agent-host cache, getSessions can kick off one guarded asynchronous refresh, but it is not awaited.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both changed context-key lines execute before menu display, and the traced helpers enumerate/materialize the complete merged collection despite needing only a boolean.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu delay depends on session-history size, number of providers, and how many trailing chats are hidden/tool-origin. The uncapped synchronous mechanism is established; prevalence at very large histories is the main uncertainty.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable performance regression: unnecessary all-history CPU/allocation is introduced on a latency-sensitive UI path, even when the setting hides the command.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Move to Session, choose a destination, and complete or undo the move
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the picker appears, destinations are enumerated and sorted. After selection, destinations are re-enumerated for validation, then one provider move is awaited before success feedback. Undo, only when explicitly selected, performs one additional move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: moveChat or moveSession to the owning agent host after the user selects one destination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one awaited IPC for the confirmed move; an explicit Undo can issue one more. There is no call per candidate destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These new commands did not exist, while the equivalent drag-and-drop operation already issued the same single move IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected move must complete before result feedback; picker enumeration itself performs no boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of compatible destination sessions; quick-pick construction is O(D log D) for D valid destinations, while destination discovery scans all known sessions. One selected move is sent regardless of D.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One command invocation awaits one move. Agent-host move operations are serialized by the host; there is no per-destination fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session providers use their existing model caches. Destination arrays and picker items are rebuilt per invocation, and the post-pick rebuild intentionally revalidates asynchronous state; no result cache is retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-IPC call path and destination cardinality; uncertain only in exact picker latency at unusually large histories.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large destination lists increase picker setup and sorting cost, but this is user-requested work and no evidence shows it exceeds the existing quick-pick pattern enough to warrant another finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the command performs bounded, expected work for an explicitly requested move and does not fan out across boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag a chat or single-chat session onto another Sessions-list row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drag-over computes one candidate target synchronously; drop calls the existing move runner and awaits one provider move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Single moveChat or moveSession operation after drop
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per completed drop, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the refactor, a completed valid drop already issued one identical provider move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after drop; no boundary is crossed merely while hovering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source and one hovered target per drag-over event. Append-anchor work scales only with the hovered target's trailing hidden/tool chats, not all sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Drag-over evaluations are synchronous and individual; a completed drop starts one move, with existing provider/host serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing session/chat observables with no new retained cache. The helper refactor creates the same destination/anchor information that the prior inline code computed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: old and new hunks perform the same validity check and append-anchor lookup for one target.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality; helper allocation differences are negligible and do not change target cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the refactor preserves work scale and boundary count.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The help content synchronously appends one additional localized paragraph before display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant: one added string independent of sessions, chats, or providers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous content construction with no queueing or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache or retained lifecycle; content remains bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff adds one bounded content.push only.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all seven changed files. Submitted one synchronous UI-work finding for uncapped destination enumeration during context-menu construction; the command, drag/drop, accessibility, tests, move IPC cardinality, cache behavior, and concurrency introduce no other high-confidence performance issue.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
